### Two-generation rollover and AAC allowance (2026-11-10)

The initial automatic two-generation synthetic fixture failed before its
second rollover: remote jobs `30103800983323089` and `30103800983323090`
reported a media preparation refusal, `Clock(Limit)`. The fixture's explicit
AAC epoch allowance was eight frames, and the longer scenario exhausted it.
That counterexample also exposed a service integration gap: the laboratory
recorder chooses a finite epoch allowance, and renewal had not been exposed
through its archive worker and guard. At typical AAC rates a fixed allowance
of one million frames lasts hours, not thirty days.

The working tree now exposes bounded renewal without resetting the existing
clock and without authorizing an archive retry. The extended fixture retains
the eight-frame counterexample, requests a renewal only after the refusal,
and then explicitly retries the same retained source. An initial strict remote
request timed out before admission on a busy worker; subsequent remote job
`30103800983323098` passed five automatic rollover tests, including two journal
generations after that refusal and renewal (82 other cases filtered). Its base
was `a978d5dd1bbfdfbba254ced7df493c4f9a73bbcc` and overlay fingerprint was
`b418dba53147afd856211597b800515618c5f3e14873b76bf6ca606a108642dc`.

A newer working-tree change adds an optional, explicitly budgeted automatic
renewal policy that checks the session before further work, preserves active
archive draining, and services control when renewal is refused or exhausted.
Remote job `30103800983323108` passed the same five targeted tests (82 filtered)
with renewal, budget exhaustion, active archive ownership and a time-sync
reply during exhaustion in the two-generation fixture. Its overlay fingerprint
was `1ca39257979a4f8ecd4c2b07b0ed8da831980031217db7d4ce402ac600fc2c51`;
the job exited zero and released both source and pair. The caller must supply
a minimum covering its maximum per-segment AAC frame count and invoke this
policy-aware step. Regression job `30103800983323110` passed 26 recording
contracts (one private-input replay ignored) and five storage-capacity
contracts; its overlay fingerprint was
`16bb14723a06ea00c6ff2673034aad34f78c2d3f89fee34b8858d01378f239a5`.
None of these results establishes unattended physical-camera
recording, live AAC timing behavior, deployed automatic renewal, restart
recovery, or 30-day retention. The AAC clock also rejects accumulated sender
drift outside its fixed jitter tolerance; extending its allowance does not
address that separate long-duration failure mode.

### Managed recording and rollover (working tree)

The working tree now has one owner for a source-aware session, the explicit
AAC renewal policy, staged successor supplies and the two-stage A/V rollover.
It delivers each normal session event before acting on a later capacity
signal. At capacity without staged stores it retains the exact predecessor and
services control; with stores it starts the preflight and successor worker,
then resumes the same session only after the checked transition. Admission
refusal requires explicit retry, and halted owners remain available for
reconciliation. Store creation, re-provisioning, restart recovery, camera
adoption and a deployed unattended service are not implemented by this owner.

### Fresh successor-store creation (working tree)

A new region-owned worker creates an exclusive private successor directory
and its empty A/V journal and keeper under a caller-bound replay root. Its
caller supplies the already-created switch with separately selected pin
custody, the filesystem capability, read policy and bounded work. It checks
task authority before admission, checks cancellation between creation stages,
and retains the original switch and any completed store owners after failure;
it neither deletes partial files nor retries a refused creation. This does not
yet construct the switch or integrate the creation worker into the managed
session, and it does not establish independent storage failure domains.

Remote job `30103800983323126` failed its initial synthetic test at task
finalization because the fixture supplied a completion timestamp earlier than
the observed runtime clock; it ran no other test (five filtered). After the
timestamp correction, an added checkpoint between root creation and parent
synchronization, and preservation of the created root and replay authority,
job `30103800983323133` passed the focused test (one passed, five filtered).
It covered invalid parent refusal, an existing-directory collision without
replacement, interruption after the first store, and a successful one-time
supplies transfer. The base was `a978d5dd1bbfdfbba254ced7df493c4f9a73bbcc`
and the overlay fingerprint was
`755179277c56b812a0866feeb0f1a25608d4f7ea556aec719abd513f4726590d`.
Both jobs were acknowledged and released their source and execution pair.
Job `30103800983323138` subsequently passed the full recording suite
(26 passed, one private replay ignored) and the storage suite (six passed),
with overlay fingerprint
`961c3125bfb981d27d9e78e7ee3ce8eb1de04bfe436ce533772901e6f3b745c8`.
That regression predates the provisioning-session integration below.

and limits remain separately recoverable. A refused start needs explicit retry;
partial creation and unaccepted ready supplies remain owned. The switch and

### Bounded rollover generation planning (working tree)

An optional in-memory plan now chooses a bounded sequence of deterministic,
exclusive successor and pin-retainer paths and domain-separated pin scopes.
Planning performs no filesystem I/O; the existing creator checks the live
task and replay authorities before creating stores. Generations share the
original replay authority objects, so their cancellation is not reset. A
collision or partial creation remains a refusal with its owners retained.
The provisioning driver reports planning, creation and exhaustion explicitly,
and will not create further stores while previous custody is unclaimed.

Job `30103800983323224` passed the focused three-transition session (one
passed, 88 filtered) with the third creator selected by this plan. It used base
`a978d5dd1bbfdfbba254ced7df493c4f9a73bbcc` and overlay fingerprint
`25e53d84b123621a753b58958b736dcd760b2d45da23b4e650aefe200f4b9d02`.
Job `30103800983323231` passed the recording suite (26 passed, one ignored)
and storage-capacity suite (six passed); the latter checks plan bounds,

Its overlay fingerprint was
`4bcb0a42128142701db801a4f12cc5b9ab2fb5ca7bc95ab10377554535515d5a`.
The expanded fixture selects two consecutive creators from the plan, completes
the third transition, checks A/V graph readback across it, and retains a fourth
set of staged stores and its custody. Job `30103800983323237` did not compile
because the new check lacked a trait import. After correcting the check, job

at overlay fingerprint
`3dab8c8e0fe7ac2fc564d297aa2c958da7e08bc3e2b31c55767796b9f2ed098c`.

The caller still configures the plan, takes custody of each created store, and
must durably reserve and recover generation choices across process restarts.
Distinct paths alone do not prove independent failure domains. These synthetic
tests do not establish a deployed, unattended recorder, physical-camera direct
capture, full-resolution recording, or 30-day retention.

The release-profile private MP4 diagnostic was compiled on Linux in strict

`yuvj420p` output. All 151 positions matched. The two measured wall times

The benchmark script's SHA-256 was
`7b42ad1ce24372498270fd010120c44dcc65ece6a11fe79d8ac02b569e8348f6`
both in this checkout and on the recorder host.

approximately 1,000 CPU-clock samples without reported loss. The approximate

changed. The existing recorder was active with zero restarts during this work.
This is offline decode of Scrypted-captured media, not direct Rust capture,
continuous recording, or evidence of 30-day retention.

### Provisioning cancellation fence (working tree)

Source inspection found that calling `ProvisioningSession::abort` before a
creator started did not prevent a later `step` from starting it. The working
tree now latches cancellation, refuses later plan and worker offers or retry
authorization, and reports an aborted step without polling the camera or
starting new work. An active creator can still be joined, and its failure or
completed but uninstalled supplies remain owned for explicit recovery. An
active rollover can likewise be joined, and the returned owners expose the
abort state. This is an in-memory cancellation boundary, not persistent
restart recovery or a deployed recorder.

The first pre-start regression attempt, job `30103800983323307`, failed
with a channel timeout before the cancellation check. Job
`30103800983323309` passed seven existing rollover cases but failed the new
case with a closed channel. The synthetic camera peer had been configured to
stop before all required control messages; neither failure proves the
suspected cancellation bug or independently pins down the timeout. The peer sequence was
corrected, and a further case was added for a creator that completes just
before abort. Job `30103800983323318` passed the seven existing cases but both
new cases failed with `automatic replay control failed` before cancellation.
Job `30103800983323319` again passed seven existing cases, while both new
cases stopped at `managed supplies wait lost control or boundary`, still
before cancellation. After correcting the peer stop point through the full
control sequence, strict-remote job `30103800983323321` passed all nine
automatic rollover cases, with 82 other tests filtered. The new cases check
abort before creation starts and abort after creation finishes but before
installation. The existing cancellation case now also removes its failed
creator from the driver and verifies that a remaining generation plan does
not start after abort. The run used base
`a978d5dd1bbfdfbba254ced7df493c4f9a73bbcc` and overlay fingerprint
`36105414b16a9a24747549ad3050da68f8d2e0c5b48c49f0de68e8bc3b4d635d`.
These are synthetic session tests. An active rollover cancelled through the
new `join_rollover` wrapper has not been separately exercised, and no physical
camera effect, unattended service or persistent restart recovery was tested.

### Controller access through managed recording (working tree)

`ManagedSession` and `ProvisioningSession` now lend the existing bounded
controller handle while the original recording session, custody preflight,
or successor rollover owns it. The handle does not transfer media or storage
ownership, and the existing effect preparation, authorization and dispatch
checks remain in force. Control is unavailable after a halted transition or
provisioning abort. The subsequent standalone managed trial described below
connects this handle to the provisioning driver.

`cc7ea9b1cc10b9a7ed8dc9f44937245be230d4d7364d27738a8eb3cabb6fd9ce`.
All three successful jobs used base

### Standalone managed trial and bounded rollover (working tree)

The standalone trial can opt into managed storage and pre-create up to eight
successor generations. An explicitly configured journal limit travels through
both storage creation and recovery. The limit must be supplied consistently;
it is not cryptographically bound to the archive. The lab's archive inspection
command currently assumes default limits. The trial's journals and pins share
one host and filesystem, so independent pin durability is unverified. Abort,
unclaimed custody and incomplete worker transitions require reconciliation;
the trial does not silently retry them.

On `ts1`, four individually executed process tests passed (one test each,
40 filtered each): managed rollover, managed event replies, legacy event
replies, and command-line rejection before I/O. The rollover fixture used a
five-record A/V history to force a boundary, published two synthetic segments,
installed a successor, resumed an already-ledgered operation, and published
a third segment with readback. It used the final trial SHA-256
`c58aeeb26f8e4ba07ea9813d95876aa465748e93680551b9d5b09058c4835c5d`
and test SHA-256
`faa292931d79981bb1a80368972fcb5e7f7f18b9ddf466ca64214864cf4bb2f9`.
The Linux build compiled in job `30103800983323362`; its wrapper returned
102 because RCH refused to install Linux artifacts on macOS. The artifacts
were copied on the Linux worker and their hashes checked before and after tests.
An earlier forced-boundary run exposed a capacity signal being treated as a
terminal error; the current trial accepts only the specific safe pre-publication
capacity signal. An earlier provisioning build also failed on an error type
conversion and was corrected before the passing build.

Job `30103800983323358` passed the storage recovery test with non-default
history limits and refused an invalid limit before archive creation. Job
`30103800983323360` passed 26 recording contracts with one private-camera test
ignored and all six storage-capacity contracts. These tests and the process
fixtures are synthetic. The trial remains time- and segment-bounded, has no
qualified persistent supervisor or complete rollover restart recovery, and
does not prove physical camera handoff, high-resolution live capture, or
continuous recording and 30-day retention.

#### Full-resolution camera-derived replay refusals (2026-11-11)

The retained five-second, video-only high-profile G4 clip still matched SHA-256
`2ce702b355fa7d8a56780a5dc881d3c0e68b5a21d2e9db7d0bd8b0cef6b55361`.
An FFmpeg stream-copy remux to FLV fed an ignored managed-trial process fixture
through private pipes and a temporary RAM filesystem. The controller was
simulated, and no camera or recorder setting was changed. The test did not
archive a segment: FFprobe showed the first two MP4 decode timestamps were
0 and 11 microseconds, both became 0 milliseconds in FLV, and the recorder
refused the resulting duplicate timeline. This finding applies to this clip
conversion, not necessarily to the camera's live FLV timestamps.

A test-only transformation changed the second video timestamp to 1 ms while
leaving the sample bytes intact. The trial then refused
`Mux(UnsupportedFormat)`. A separate in-memory NAL inventory found two SPS
and two PPS repetitions in the samples, each byte-equal to its declared
configuration; the current FLV AVC muxer does not accept those in-band types.
The muxer uses an `avc1` sample entry; in-band parameter-set carriage calls
for a deliberate container and provenance design (see the W3C discussion of
[`avc1` and `avc3`](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=22136)),
not a silent relaxation of the refusal. Removing only those four matching
parameter sets in the test stream led to a third refusal, `Media(NoAudio)`:
the current A/V bootstrap needs an audio witness even for this clip's
video-only path. This transformation is not production behavior and does not
qualify the original footage, timestamps, or an audio track.

The new high-resolution process case remains ignored and is a failing
acceptance test for this input, not a passing result. The trial now reports a
payload-free media-error stage and typed framing or recording reason to make
these failures actionable. The final trial and fixture hashes on `ts1` were
`1331b00f4f2818d23c98c693298119a05f72b88ac10980b153c14751825f1301`
and `aee78eeea76fca4b624b78340c853bd2645e5b03e6cc48b2bf29c139c21fa00a`.
The Linux build compiled in job `30103800983323382`; RCH returned 102 because
it refused to install Linux artifacts on macOS. On that build, repeated
rollover, managed event-reply and legacy event-reply fixtures each passed
when run sequentially (one passed, 42 filtered each). An initial concurrent
run collided on a fixed fixture port and did not pass; the sequential runs do
not establish concurrent fixture safety. The real recorder remained active.

#### Explicit in-band AVC recording (working tree, 2026-11-11)

An opt-in `avc3` FLV muxer now accepts in-band SPS and PPS only before a
picture and only when their bytes exactly match the source configuration. It
copies those NALs into the fragment with original-byte mappings. Changed
parameter sets still refuse without advancing the fragment cursor. The legacy
`avc1` constructor retains its prior refusal. The `avc3` choice travels
through the recording owner, A/V initialization and source-checked archive
readback; archive verification also compares in-band parameter sets to the
retained source configuration. The laboratory opts in with `--lab-inband-avc`.
This is a fixed-configuration profile, not general midstream configuration
change support or evidence of automatic camera negotiation.

Strict-remote container job `30103800983323393` passed nine contracts with one

#### Video-only archival without an AAC hypothesis (working tree)

segment, and publishes the existing unknown-time video evidence graph through

clock, or physical capture time is supplied. The caller must supervise and
authorize the synchronous work, retain the returned source and receipt, keep
the same storage owners across explicit reconciliation, and drain all owners
on cancellation. A denied or uncertain publication retains the same segment

not provide a supervised long-running worker, persistent restart recovery,
independently powered anchors or a retention policy.

#### Cancellation-drained video-only worker (working tree)

`video_worker` now wraps the video-only sink and its dedicated deployment,
unknown-time journal, keeper and replay authority in one task-admitted worker.
It checks the task clock and stage/publish grants before starting a bounded
blocking attempt. It keeps a pending segment through refusal and cancellation,
returns the original segment and actual receipt on success, and joins before
retirement. A runtime error or panic fences the owner; retirement retains any
unclaimed report and storage owners for reconciliation. The worker reports
payload-free failure categories and preserves an actual post-publication
receipt rather than sending non-thread-safe archive errors across the worker.
It does not itself establish independent anchor durability, automatically
roll over a full journal, recover after process restart, or supervise a camera.

### Video-only supervised session (2026-11-11)

`video_session` connects an already admitted supervisor to distinct video and
separate-source archive workers. It pauses media reads while a source is
retained or an archive attempt runs, but continues bounded control polling.
Each result or completion remains caller-owned. A refusal or failed start
requires an explicit retry decision, and cancellation requires both workers to
drain before recovering their owners. Attachment requires idle workers and the
same caller-supplied source key as the video sink; source identity remains a
claim, and the caller must bind the original configuration to the connection.

### Source-preserving shutdown tail (working tree)

The video-only path now separates unfinished framed records from unframed
framer or socket bytes. `retirement_source::Plan` validates ordered offsets
against bytes actually received before moving the originals; refusal returns
the complete retirement unchanged. The source evidence graph records whether
bytes were held in an unfinished fragment or remained unframed, including the
claimed local unframed origin. It makes no tag-boundary or capture-time claim
for unframed bytes. A task-owned driver offers and archives the ranges in order,
requires explicit retry after a refused attempt, and retains its owners until
each task drains. The bounded trial now archives the resulting tail and checks
source metadata on readback. An incomplete GOP remains source data rather than
a fabricated playable segment; bytes never received from the socket remain
unknown. A failure can still end the laboratory process with unpersisted
in-memory owners, and no continuous service, rollover or 30-day retention is
established.

#### Region-owned video rollover checks (2026-11-11)

The video predecessor can now be checked on a region-owned blocking worker
while the original pending source remains in the borrowed retirement. A
single-use observation binds the scope, confirmed root, journal and keeper
heads, and prior transition count before transfer. The video rollover worker
then stages and commits the successor, rechecks read and retention authority,
replays the confirmed root, and prepares attachment. The pending source stays
owned across denied replay; the checked successor can attach only after a
successful drained task result. Storage panics and uncertain outcomes remain
fenced for reconciliation. These workers do not themselves provision storage,
continue camera control, or automatically resume a recording session.

after reporting exhaustion and after creator results, failures and custody
have been transferred. Cancellation prevents renewal. This is an in-memory
authorization, not persisted restart recovery, automatic unbounded creation,

### Retained generation reservation foundation (2026-11-11)

`ReservedPlan` now binds a generation plan to a dedicated, separately
retained journal. It durably appends the selected deterministic generation
identity before returning its unstarted storage creator. A reservation
remains pending until the caller records an exact-identity reconciliation
reference. The reference is a caller assertion: the component does not
validate its contents, prove physical storage independence, or settle a camera
effect. Reopen checks the exact retained head, canonical history, contiguous
generations, deterministic identity and immutable configuration fingerprint.
Storage or cancellation failures fence the owner; an unstarted creator selected
before a refusal is returned for reconciliation. The in-memory batch extension
is still separately caller-authorized.

The synchronous reservation API performs storage I/O and requires a drained,
region-owned blocking worker. Such a worker and the provisioning-session
integration do not yet exist; existing managed trials continue to use their
volatile plan. The test drops and reopens filesystem owners within the same
process, rather than demonstrating process crash, physical power loss, a live
camera handoff, or a deployable restart service. It does not settle either
previously indeterminate physical-camera effect.

reconciliation, a storage-capacity fence, and cancellation immediately after

`3626fdfe5dbfeff3f6b40059d32607be0b78d56256a4a7d4f1402204e6b7e092`;
the job exited zero, acknowledged its result and released its sources and

### Region-owned reservation worker (2026-11-11)

A single-use `ReservationWorker` now runs the retained plan's reservation
or caller-attested reconciliation operation on a drained Asupersync blocking
worker. The caller supplies separate task resources and replay contexts for
journal and pin custody; those labels do not prove physical independence or
that the underlying storage capability uses the asserted paths. Cancellation
is checked before and after journal writes, and the original plan, request,
selected unstarted creator, and actual outcome remain owned until join and
retirement. Cancellation, runtime failure, panic or inconsistent state fences
the retired plan for cold reconciliation. The reconciliation digest remains
a caller-supplied reference, not verification of its contents.

### Bounded local creator observation (2026-11-11)

additional generations. After a managed creator is drained and reports a

the next generation may be reserved. Recovery checks that binding. Creator
custody is retained in a bounded owner queue; cancellation or mismatches retain
owners and fence advancement. This observation is local completion evidence,

### Renewable local-observation allowance (2026-11-11)

The retained video session now offers an explicit in-memory renewal for one
to eight further generations after its earlier finite allowance is spent. It
requires the successful local creator observation to have been journaled at

head, and unsettled owners. It constructs an unstarted reservation worker;

### Native full-size video still (2026-11-11)

`video_still::from_picture` joins an already decoded H.264 picture to the
first-party JPEG encoder without resizing or external media frameworks. The
caller must select BT.601 full or limited range; the H.264 decoder does not
expose VUI color metadata, so this is a declared transform, not an inferred
camera claim. Conversion uses bounded dimensions and pixel work, checks the
expected I420 digest, and observes cancellation during hashing, conversion
and JPEG encoding. The immutable result binds the picture-plane digest,
declared transform, pixel digest, encoder identity and JPEG digest. It is a
lossy derivative, not source custody, privacy/export approval, physical
camera identity, or evidence of capture time. The function performs no I/O
and has not yet been connected to a live snapshot endpoint or supervisor.

### Source-checked archive still and drained worker (2026-11-11)

transform and still identity. The recovered pin is a past read observation, not

atomic policy snapshot, and cancellation is not preemptive inside one H.264

continuous camera service or a user-visible export endpoint.

### Opt-in still export and private G4 replay (2026-11-11)

The bounded trial accepts an explicit `--lab-save-still=ABSOLUTE_PATH` after

decode enabled. It checks the exact read and storage grants, rechecks read
policy and cancellation during chunked staging, writes a mode-0600 file in a
private destination directory, syncs it, publishes via a no-replace hard link,
and drains the blocking worker. An ambiguous link result retains staging for
inspection; successful linking with uncertain cleanup or directory sync is
reported separately. The filesystem calls use path names, not directory-fd
anchored traversal; the caller must use a trusted private path whose ancestors
cannot be replaced concurrently. The policy and cancellation checks are
sequential, not atomic with publication; revocation can race the final link.

snapshot endpoint, a stable latest-frame service, or a production deployment.

### Periodic scanner enrollment handoff (2026-11-11)

A running fleet scanner can now be parked, releasing its fleet borrow while
retaining its configured scan scope, original task and runtime, next due time,
and interrupted phase. The owner may add a separately supplied enrollment to
the same fleet and resume the token. A token cannot resume on another fleet;
refusal returns the token unchanged. An interrupted observation remains fenced
until explicitly acknowledged. This closes the in-process borrow conflict
between repeated discovery and adding an enrollment; it does not create a
certificate pin or credential from unauthenticated network claims, schedule a
setup, automate Wi-Fi provisioning, or persist inventory across restart.

policy/cancellation checks remain sequential rather than atomic with linking;

### Bounded confirmed-segment history pages (2026-11-11)

The unknown-time publication journal can enumerate confirmed segment pins in
bounded pages anchored to an exact verified prefix. Subsequent appends do not
change a saved prefix. The API validates the cursor, semantic prepare/confirm
sequence and prefix membership, checks cancellation while scanning, and reports
any unconfirmed intent separately. It scans the bounded journal for each page;
it does not verify the corresponding media, establish independent pin custody,
or traverse rollover generations. The existing video trial now compares its
current generation's paged history to the suffix of its published pins and
requires the keeper to match that prefix before its separate archive readback.
Earlier generations are explicitly reported as not enumerated. The trial still
has its eight-segment cap and is not a continuous recorder.

### Verified cross-generation history (2026-11-11)

A settled in-memory rollover custody can now provide a bounded history view
across its retained predecessor journals and current successor. Creating the
view checks the retained switch chain and keeper heads, verifies each old
confirmed root and the exact seeded successor prefix, and refuses pending or
unreconciled current history. Each page contains at most 128 confirmations and
labels each item with its local generation and record sequence. The first
verified successor seed is excluded at each boundary; later repeated roots are
not silently removed. Cursors belong to one view and cannot be used in another.
A full page at a generation boundary may have a final empty continuation. The
view borrows the owners and therefore does not read concurrently with their
mutation; it neither discovers/reopens a chain after restart nor verifies media,
physical time, independent custody or uninterrupted coverage.

run. Strict-remote `ts1` job `30105869848936564` passed eight journal/rollover

### Refreshable routing hints after setup (2026-11-12 UTC)

A completed discovery window can now refresh the untrusted source-address hint
for a finished fleet entry whose setup permits a connection attempt. The
original setup report, candidate index, operation identity and unresolved
effect remain unchanged. Missing or conflicting claims suspend new routes
until a later unconflicted window. A pending early socket is refused if its
source no longer matches the latest hint when setup finishes. Existing routed
sockets are not evicted by discovery alone. In-flight or interrupted setup
claims are not replaced, and no management operation is retried. The refreshed
address is not identity proof: listener admission must explicitly permit the
new address and the peer must still be authenticated independently. A scoped
window may miss a present camera and can therefore temporarily suspend a
reconnect; it does not establish absence.

### Coordinated discovery and routing pump (2026-11-12 UTC)

A caller-owned discovery pump now composes an existing periodic scanner and
bounded controller router using the exact same fleet and task clock mapping.
It retains one scan future and the router's in-flight owners across events,
alternates first polling preference, and spawns no detached tasks. Dropping a
`next` future preserves them. A requested scan stop does not start another
window and allows the current one to drain; an observation error stops new
scans until explicitly resumed, and an interrupted scanner still requires its
existing acknowledgement. Dropping the pump during a probe leaves the
scanner interrupted; the caller still owns and must retire the router, handle
every event and authenticate and supervise routed peers. This is orchestration
composition, not automatic setup, a running daemon, crash recovery or native
recording. The module is a new untracked source file in the shared tree.

### Bounded independent camera work (2026-11-12 UTC)

The discovery pump now exposes a bounded caller-owned camera work set. It
accepts at most one future per enrollment index, returns the exact future on
duplicate or capacity refusal, keeps pending futures when a wait is dropped,
and returns pending work to the caller for explicit retirement. It preserves
round-robin order when a completed camera immediately resubmits; using
swap-remove here could otherwise starve another ready camera. No task is
spawned, and each future must retain its own session and effect authority.
Dropping the set itself interrupts its futures and may leave effects requiring
reconciliation. This is a building block, not an unattended supervisor or
a claim that two real cameras have been enrolled or recorded.

### Task-bound retry timers in the discovery pump (2026-11-12 UTC)

An owner can schedule a completed, proven pre-effect setup failure in a bounded
retry queue. It uses configurable exponential backoff with a finite retry count,
binds each timer to the exact failed operation, and rechecks that marker before
rearming. A pending route delays rearming; a stale timer cannot rearm a later
attempt. The queue shares the discovery pump's fleet, task and clock mapping.
Dropping a wait retains its timer, and the pump can keep driving discovery or
controller routing while a retry waits. The owner still has to schedule a
failure, resolve credentials, create fresh transport and start the new setup;
the timer does not grant effect authority or provide an unattended service.

Strict-remote ts1 job `30105869848936692` passed all 21 selected discovery,
fleet, retry-policy and work-set unit tests. Job `30105869848936697` passed
the selected synthetic camera HTTP/controller fixture (1 test, three scenarios),
including backoff, dropped-wait retention, duplicate scheduling, pump-driven
rearming and a fresh setup. Both used base
`9b5bfd56e5cd441d44c02a0d3b516663ad14fb37` and overlay
`9c87ff3292a869bf78d58132f19f1d9ed40fcf9776030ad8c9f1a7fdbb0599da`;
both exited zero, acknowledged terminal results, and released source and pair
custody. No physical camera effect was attempted. The existing trj recorder and

Direct ownership, unattended onboarding, production TLS, continuous native

### Coordinated setup completion and retry admission (2026-11-12 UTC)

The discovery pump can now drive bounded camera setup futures, retry timers,
discovery and controller routing together. When a setup returns a failure, it
automatically schedules a retry only if the operation matches the fleet's
current proven pre-effect failure. The event retains the original outcome and
reports whether timer admission succeeded or was refused. An existing timer
for a different operation is not silently replaced. Setup work, timer waits and
scan/route owners remain caller-owned across a dropped wait; the loop alternates
its preference so ready setup work cannot indefinitely starve pump events.

### Camera connections waiting for a lease (2026-11-12 UTC)

one-use TLS lease is being acquired. It registers at most one waiting handshake
per resource, wakes it on installation, rechecks task and route authority on
poll, and removes the registration when the handshake is dropped. The existing
acceptor deadline bounds the wait. A stale registration caused by reentrant
drop is reclaimable by a successor; a concurrently live competitor is refused.

### Scoped P-256 client and live TLS-only observation (2026-11-12 UTC)

The experimental client now implements task-scoped P-256 ECDH as well as
X25519. It obtains a fixed-width scalar from the existing per-connection entropy
source, bounds rejection sampling, emits an uncompressed SEC1 point and refuses
invalid peer points. The camera TLS configuration permits one explicitly
selected group; it does not automatically discover group compatibility. The
new direct `p256` dependency is confined to this non-production laboratory.

The first TLS-only G4 probe, configured for X25519, failed its handshake. An
independent OpenSSL check also failed with only X25519, while P-256 succeeded
and the observed certificate matched the previously retained network pin.
After the scoped P-256 change, a TLS-only probe from ts1 to the observed G4
completed TLS 1.3 with that pin and verified the server handshake signature.
It sent no HTTP request or credentials and made no settings change. The same
probe's independent disposable P-256 server fixture passed matching-pin and
wrong-pin cases, observing zero application bytes. The first fixture version
returned a server-side BrokenPipe while it attempted to issue TLS tickets; the
reported fixture result uses a no-ticket server and successful completed runs.

Strict-remote ts1 test job `30106308287922255` passed 33/33 tests
(12+4+1+4+4+4+4), including P-256 agreement, malformed-point and invalid
scalar refusals and pinned-client success and wrong-pin refusal. It exited
zero, was acknowledged and released source and pair. Its source overlay
fingerprint was `e8a719bdae713628684f4c633d81b0e121a7b07cea731a10aa662f95757bd087`.
Build job `30106308287922256` completed remotely with exit zero; its wrapper
returned 102 because RCH rejected installing a Linux binary on macOS. Its
terminal result was acknowledged and source and pair were released. The Linux
probe used for fixture and G4 checks had SHA-256
`dc7a0f12aa48b6fc4a124aac0998e50ebe4d33e90ca730dd527051003c29aadb`,
matched before and after the live check. The observed network certificate
digest was `f266d3f9dbede6c30bc062c2d06d0b8091431d8347e5c6898de5ed09832bae36`.
The recorder and both relevant timers were active with NRestarts=0 afterward.

This is an actual-camera TLS handshake, not a login, video stream, physical
identity authentication, production TLS admission, automatic setup or a

### Task-scoped setup-to-controller bridge (2026-11-12 UTC)

The scoped TLS lab now exposes a reusable setup-to-controller upgrade path
for an eventual executable. It runs the existing tracked setup and accept
once, then uses one already-drained task-bound entropy lease per controller
TLS attempt. Only an early TLS EOF may admit a fresh connection from the
selected source claim; it never replays setup. The caller retains unused
leases, the setup trace and the effect journal, including on failure or
cancellation. Before setup, the bridge rejects invalid bounds, mismatched
leases, an already-scoped TLS configuration and enabled TLS tickets.
Neither the source/MAC claims nor a successful upgrade authenticate the
physical camera or reconcile its handoff.

### Bounded automatic retries for fleet setup (2026-11-12 UTC)

The fleet now separates an explicitly requested retry before an effect from
automatic retry. Only a returned, pre-effect timeout or selected transient
connection error is automatically scheduled for the exact completed operation.
Credential, authorization, malformed-response and unavailable-profile
refusals are not automatically retried. A prepared or interrupted effect is
not made retryable by this classification. Explicit retry retains the existing
pre-effect, operation-identity and bounded-attempt checks.

On ts1, the selected reference tests passed (one classification test, one
rearm-state test, seven standard setup cases and three separately invoked
worker-interface cases). A synthetic fleet test passed four scenarios,
including an EOF automatically retried, a 403 refused automatic retry but
explicitly scheduled, and synthetic full-resolution video. The detailed job
and source receipts are in the lab README under “Automatic retry classification.”
These are synthetic results, not proof of camera identity, direct G4 video,
production TLS, uninterrupted recording or 30-day retention. A connection
failure during login may leave a camera session whose expiry is unknown.

### Stream completion fence (2026-11-12 UTC)

The experimental automatic stream owner now fences a completed stream until
its exact owner-bound completion is explicitly released after reconciliation.
Another routed session for that camera is returned to the caller while the
completion remains unresolved. Running automatic work and unresolved
completions also prevent `into_pending` from discarding that owner. The
release method checks token ownership and freshness; the caller is responsible
for the actual reconciliation evidence and authority.

Strict-remote ts1 job `30106308287922392` passed 17/17 lab library tests and
the four-scenario synthetic fleet test. The fixture decoded a synthetic
2688 x 1512 stream and then refused a reconnect while its effects remained
unresolved; it also tested stopped-owner and retained-work paths. This fence
is process-local: a different owner, the unrestricted insertion path, a
process restart, or a dropped owner can bypass its state. It is not durable
restart recovery, automatic reconciliation, direct G4 capture, continuous
recording or 30-day retention. Details are in the lab README under “Stream
completion fence.”

### Retaining the media listener for later connections (2026-11-12 UTC)

The upstream direct-stream implementation describes cameras making multiple
short-lived TCP connections before a stable media push
(https://github.com/xuio/scrypted-unifi-direct/blob/main/src/direct-stream.ts).
This is an interoperability hypothesis for the G4, not an observation that
the earlier physical G4 failure was caused by this behavior.

The Rust media listener now offers a task-scoped `accept_next` with exclusive
mutable borrowing, retaining the same bound port after an accepted, denied, or
cancelled accept. The original one-shot `accept` remains available. A new
`start_before_reply_retaining_listener` returns the first pipeline with the
listener so a caller may account for a failed candidate and accept another.
The caller supplies fresh per-connection source keys and owns retirement; this
does not itself choose a healthy candidate, bound the total number of attempts,
reconcile control effects, recover on restart, or constitute an always-on
service. Cancellation of a pending accept consumes its framer and recorder.

### Bounded empty-media candidate selection (2026-11-12 UTC)

The task-owned TCP ingress can now reserve and read only the first byte of a
fresh source. The UniFi ingress retains that byte at offset zero in its framer;
the pipeline distinguishes a zero-byte EOF from data without transferring or
losing the byte. An interrupted pending probe retains its prepaid one-byte
reservation. Audio tracking can still be enabled after a successful first-byte
probe, because no FLV record has yet been parsed.

`MediaCandidates` owns the retained listener and current pipeline, enforces a
finite overall deadline and candidate count, and advances automatically only
after a zero-byte EOF. It refuses reused source keys and preserves the current
pipeline after a stalled or failed probe. A byte is not proof of valid FLV,
healthy video, or physical identity; the caller still validates and retains
subsequent records. The bounded scoped trial uses the selector for its
media-before-reply path, including event-aware setup, and uses the selected
connection key for its archive. It does not service controller messages while
selection is pending; a camera waiting for such a reply can reach the deadline.
This remains a bounded experimental trial, not an autonomous service, durable
recovery, direct physical G4 capture, or 30-day retention.

denied peers, cancellation/resume, exact first-byte custody, a one-byte budget
reservation without double charging, audio setup, maximum candidates and

contracts (three owner-input cases ignored) and 1/1 initial probe contract.
Job `30106308287922436` passed 2/2 synthetic-controller cases (111 filtered)

### Controller service while selecting media candidates (2026-11-12 UTC)

The candidate selector can now run alongside the same task-bound controller
session. While it waits, it services bounded camera clock requests and optional
startup event replies using the original operation lists, journal and traces.
It verifies the task, runtime, clock and already-used operation identities.
An interrupted or failed reply leaves `selection_reply_in_flight` set and
fences a later selection using that trace; the retained effect still requires
reconciliation. The caller retains the selector and any current pipeline on
selection failure, and a captured event returned directly by a session is
returned in the error rather than silently discarded. A negative stream-setting
reply stops selection after retaining the observation. These are local protocol
facts, not proof of remote effect, physical identity or valid media.

The scoped trial uses this control-aware selector. It also passes the digests
of already-answered startup events into the video and A/V archive paths so

a pending or unselected socket is not classified as empty. The scoped trial
reports an explicit omission and unknown unread byte count before retiring such
an unselected pipeline. This is a selection policy, not camera authentication,
valid media, continuous coverage, or a safe retry of an indeterminate effect.
The one-byte probe remains resumable after cancellation. The default sequential
path remains available; the experimental trial opts into parallel selection.

### Structural header selection for concurrent media connections (2026-11-12 UTC)

The optional parallel candidate selector can now require a complete structural
FLV header before selecting a connection. The framer previews the header
without consuming it, rejects an invalid signature or version as soon as it
can, and otherwise checks the declared header length and initial size field.
The byte-at-a-time TCP probe retains its prepaid reservation on cancellation;
round-robin polling and cooperative yields let other candidates and controller
traffic make progress. Invalid or incomplete candidates remain owned for
explicit disposition, and the experimental trial reports their admitted bytes
as omitted with unread bytes unknown. Exhaustion has a distinct
`NoValidHeader` outcome. The normal sequential and first-byte selection modes
remain available. A valid header is not camera authentication, valid later
media, or proof of uninterrupted coverage.

### Deadline checks between effect preparation and commit (2026-11-12 UTC)

after durable preparation, after approval, and immediately before commit. If
the deadline has expired, the prepared effect and obligation remain in the
coordinator and must be reconciled; the controller issues no committed permit
and makes no dispatch. If commit has already begun when the deadline expires,
the prior post-commit check still retains the committed but unwritten permit.

These checks do not make storage nonblocking or explain the prior timeouts.

### Bounded prepared setup queue (2026-11-12 UTC)

The TLS lab now provides a fleet-bound queue of caller-prepared setup futures.
It checks the exact enrollment, reserves each operation ID for the lifetime
of the queue, selects the oldest work for a ready camera, and returns refused
or still-pending futures to their caller. The existing automatic supervisor
can use its `take` method as a setup factory, and only the existing retry
scheduler decides whether an attempt is eligible. A queued future remains a
caller claim: the queue cannot prove that it uses the supplied operation ID,
authenticate a camera, create credentials, reconcile effects, or preserve its

### Camera-specific prepared setup (2026-11-12 UTC)

The scoped TLS lab now constructs queued camera setup work from caller-supplied
bindings and a retained one-shot `Attempt`. The constructor uses the same
operation ID for the queue completion and the setup call. It creates one
entropy acquisition only after the future is polled; its trace, worker and
deadline-settlement result remain in the caller-owned attempt. Busy owner,
spool or attempt borrows refuse before entropy acquisition. A started attempt
cannot be polled again, and after an interrupted wait the caller can abort and
join its retained worker. The caller must still retain the owners, reconcile
effects, supply enrollment, credentials, certificate and authorities, and
decide whether a new operation is authorized. Shared `Rc<RefCell<_>>` guards
span the lab wait; this is not a production concurrency, restart or physical
identity guarantee. The factory uses one acquisition per attempt; bounded
fleet retries are separate attempts with fresh operation IDs.

### Full-resolution A/V rollover replay budget (2026-11-13 UTC)

An automatic synthetic full-resolution A/V scenario now forces a journal
capacity boundary and requires successor preflight, replay of the confirmed
predecessor, resumption, subsequent publication and archive readback. The
first direct runs failed after the successor switch. More specific error
classification showed that predecessor replay exhausted its four-billion-unit
work budget; that failure was not a cancellation and the limit was not raised.

Archive reads previously reserved work as though every spool child were the
maximum permitted object size. They now use the staged or recovered index's
payload length as a tighter read ceiling, charge for the lookup, and pass the
same ceiling to the physical read. The index is not treated as proof of file
contents: the bounded read still checks the complete envelope and digest and
refuses an enlarged replacement. A separate worker error variant preserves
budget exhaustion instead of conflating it with cancellation.

authority, and returns the checked pin without publishing or issuing a
receipt. Absence of a replay fence alone does not prove replay or custody.

### Opening switches from a retained reservation inventory (2026-11-13 UTC)

The retained generation plan can now open a complete inventory of up to 128
candidate switches using the deterministic journal and pin paths. The caller
explicitly trusts the configured candidate pin stores, supplies read limits,
and must exclude concurrent writers. The opener charges those read ceilings
before opening and checks the reservation inventory again afterward. A missing
or uncommitted candidate, including a pending reservation, is a refusal rather
than evidence that no switch exists. Refusals retain previously opened owners
and any partially bound journal or retainer. Selection checks that the same
complete reservation inventory is still current before and after comparing

16 eligible pin-probe candidates. It now allows at most 64 candidates, with
up to 128 datagrams in the two-second discovery window. Reaching the datagram

serial and authority-scoped; the limit remains finite, a slow or interrupted
scan can fail, and unreachable or unobserved duplicate certificates cannot be
ruled out. A broadcast claim is not physical identity, and this change does
not automatically enroll an unpinned device.

network namespace then fed that capture to the same hash-verified Rust
listener, which assembled a 150-sample segment and decoded a 2688 x 1512
picture. The socket used loopback, but the namespace was the existing shared
controller namespace, not a newly isolated one. The first fresh-feed attempt
failed before capture because the local FFmpeg rejected `-rw_timeout`; a
separate read check and the retry above succeeded after removing the option.
The fresh capture was replayed after collection rather than streamed directly
into Rust as it arrived. It was not saved, and no camera setting was changed
for this check. Scrypted and FFmpeg remained in the source path, and no audio,
direct live Rust connection, long-running continuity, or retention was proved.
The recorder and fallback timer remained active with restart count 2.

### Passive high-profile extended-FLV replay (2026-11-13 UTC)

A read-only capture observed the existing high-track TCP push while the
controller and recorder stayed running. One private source was selected from
the established high-track socket; the IP association is not physical-device
authentication. The capture began midstream and was reconstructed in memory.
Its final 15-second run found one contiguous TCP payload run and 688 structural
tag candidates, including 33 metadata-kind candidates; 687 gaps between
consecutive candidates were nonempty, with the largest 16 bytes. Candidate
boundaries and metadata kinds remain heuristic, not authenticated records.
None of those metadata candidates contained the literal `streamName`; because
the capture began midstream, that observation says nothing about what was sent
at connection startup. A [separate controller author reports](https://github.com/AlexxIT/go2rtc/issues/2457)
that their camera supplies the requested stream name in incoming metadata;
its presence and format on this G4 remain unverified.

The capture's selected original camera bytes, including their inter-tag data,
were sent over loopback in a newly isolated network namespace to the
hash-verified `live_media_probe`. Because the capture started midstream, the
test synthesized an FLV header, an AVC configuration from the existing relay's
SDP, one inter-tag pad, and the start boundary at a structurally identified
IDR. Matching SDP reads bracketed the capture but cannot establish the source
configuration epoch. The Rust listener assembled a 150-sample segment and
decoded a 2688 x 1512 picture. The video and packet bytes stayed in memory,
and no camera setting was changed. This is physical-camera-derived native
extended-FLV media through the Rust listener, not a live camera-to-Rust
connection, authenticated identity, control handoff, audio test, or continuous
recording. The final audit helper, outside the repository at
`work/g4-high-passive-metadata.py`, had SHA-256
`46dc18eafe7b1e29222e350319c972968c567a6c411b1b917fe1245980a0088c`.
An earlier metadata-only capture and an earlier replay with the prior helper
revision also completed. The recorder and fallback timer were active after
the final run, with restart count 2.

The preparation manifest also includes `trial_auto_setup_fixture.py` so a

validator now checks statically named same-directory Python imports as well
as Rust modules and literal includes. The complete manifest passed, and an
omitted `trial_profile_fixture` dependency was rejected. This static check
does not prove dynamic imports, external helpers, or automatic camera setup.
One fresh workspace was prepared successfully, and its copies of the setup

### Bounded script-metadata claims (2026-11-13 UTC)

`fss_packet::extended_flv::metadata` now interprets a bounded subset of AMF0
script data as a borrowed event name and optional top-level `streamName` claim.
It supports object and ECMA-array roots, ordinary primitive and bounded nested
values, and the `@setDataFrame` wrapper. Unsupported value types, malformed or
trailing data, duplicate names, excessive nesting and oversized inputs refuse
without returning partial claims. Debug output redacts both strings. The
record-facing entry point borrows the original `SourceRecord` and refuses a
provisional boundary. A nonprovisional boundary and the metadata itself remain
untrusted; no listener, fleet selector, camera identity, or authorization is
automatically changed by this parser. The AMF framing is based on the
[AMF0 specification](https://rtmp.veriskope.com/pdf/amf0-file-format-specification.pdf),
not a claim that every camera uses this profile.

Strict-remote job `30097323753213243`, source commit
`49bb5cebb990cb25f7b5afdc87f90effa5b22989`, passed six synthetic tests, with
one private-input test ignored. Its wrapper exited zero, acknowledged the
terminal result, and released source and pair. The Rust metadata source and

`8bb8b9f0cc8602f357ff3a2159fc32af1014a9ce1e508edae4f2dc5d56370c21` and
`c2819156d87c54e68687fc9dcb142ab65bdc0fcc51e17692ddbfef6c6a59c2f1`.
An earlier five-test build passed; a later `hz4` attempt stopped before Cargo

The exact test executable, SHA-256

### Non-consuming startup name inspection (2026-11-13 UTC)

The packet framer can now inspect a bounded initial prefix for a caller-chosen
AMF0 event and 16-character stream-name claim without consuming or copying
its source bytes. It returns distinct matching, mismatching, incomplete and
bound-reached outcomes, rejects provisional framing and unsupported metadata,
and debits caller-supplied work. The successor search is shared with ordinary
framing so both honor the same explicit trailer policy. The caller must retain
the source, establish connection-specific expectations and supervise repeated
work. A matching claim is unauthenticated and is not proof of camera identity.

Strict-remote job `30097323753213252`, source commit
`a17e8dac50dcfb8d0cd13dd4899b407a2b7426d0`, passed 11 metadata tests and 14
existing stream-framing tests; one owner-private metadata test was ignored.
The job exited zero, acknowledged termination, and released its source and
pair. The tested stream and test sources had SHA-256
`ce8378c48f244c65caf06e9139bc38fcc1beba9ca333d63c8a7d902e2ce63485` and
`58b3ea5d6de832e583edf82a1f92ef06d73dcfa54c27f0c13ff4d399f87f8bbb`.
The tests include every byte boundary, preservation of the original source,
mismatched names, exhausted work, unsupported metadata and provisional
boundaries. This is a synchronous packet-layer facility: it is not yet wired
into the Asupersync listener or automatic candidate selection, and no G4
connection-start metadata or direct live camera handoff was tested here.
